title: Weighted Boxes Fusion: Ensembling boxes from different object detection models
why_relevant: WBF is a strong, reproducible way to ensemble multiple detectors and often improves COCO-style mAP on Kaggle detection tasks.
extracted_technique: Fuse overlapping boxes per class by IoU clustering and confidence-weighted averaging of coordinates/scores instead of suppressing boxes (NMS).
takeaway: WBF is widely used in Kaggle to boost mAP and stabilize predictions across model seeds/sizes; it’s a natural fit for ensembling YOLO outputs in normalized coordinates.

title: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
why_relevant: The competition’s detection metric uses COCO-style mAP@[0.5:0.95], so aligning offline validation with COCO definitions is essential for correct evaluation and tuning.
extracted_technique: Evaluate detections across multiple IoU thresholds (0.50:0.95) to compute mAP; report aggregated precision/recall behavior rather than single-threshold AP.
takeaway: Use COCO-style mAP for validation to avoid optimizing the wrong objective; this matters when tuning confidence thresholds, NMS/WBF, and augmentation regimes.

title: YOLO Annotation Format
why_relevant: The dataset uses YOLO label files and the submission requires normalized center-format boxes, so correctness of coordinate transforms and formatting is a frequent failure mode.
extracted_technique: Represent boxes as normalized (x_center, y_center, width, height) in [0,1]; convert safely between xywh and xyxy for fusion and metric computation.
query: YOLO annotation format x y w h normalized
takeaway: A correct, clipped conversion layer (xywhn↔xyxy) and a strict prediction_string serializer are mandatory to prevent silent metric loss or invalid submissions.

title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
why_relevant: `right_place` is extremely imbalanced; focal loss is a common technique for class imbalance if an image classifier or meta-classifier is attempted as an ablation.
extracted_technique: Down-weight easy negatives and focus learning on hard examples via (1−p)^γ scaling; combine with class weights/oversampling carefully.
takeaway: Focal loss can help in imbalanced settings, but with only 5 positives it’s safer to default to detection-derived geometry rules and treat learned classifiers as optional ablations.
